title: publish.yml: deploy_templates job fails on release because Cloudflare secrets don't reach the called workflow
reason: The two comments explain why environment-only Cloudflare credentials cannot be passed to the reusable workflow and confirm #10649 moved deployment into an environment-bound job, which has since succeeded.
assessment: This concerns tldraw.com's Cloudflare template deployment and GitHub environment secrets. Varve's release pipeline does not call that hosted workflow or share its secret boundary.

varveAssessment.assessment: This concerns tldraw.com's Cloudflare template deployment and GitHub environment secrets. Varve's release pipeline does not call that hosted workflow or share its secret boundary.

title: Release notes workflow commits any file the agent leaves behind
reason: Reports the tldraw release-notes automation using git add -A and porcelain status rather than scoping output to its owned content. No comments were available.
assessment: Varve's release workflow builds release notes as an artifact from the approved changelog and manifest; no agent-generated release-notes job stages all repository files. The reported workflow leak has no local counterpart.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve's release workflow builds release notes as an artifact from the approved changelog and manifest; no agent-generated release-notes job stages all repository files. The reported workflow leak has no local counterpart.

title: An open menu is dropped from the registry when its owner re-renders
reason: The report identifies an effect-cleanup race between a reactive global open-menu registry and a ref used to restore the controlled state. No comments were available.
assessment: Varve menus are controlled by their owning component and portal lifecycle; the cited dual registry/ref protocol is not present. Separately tracked wheel pass-through parity from #10624 is an event-routing issue and does not imply this open-state race.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve menus are controlled by their owning component and portal lifecycle; the cited dual registry/ref protocol is not present. Separately tracked wheel pass-through parity from #10624 is an event-routing issue and does not imply this open-state race.

title: Add scheduled capacity scaling for production view-syncers
reason: Requests time-of-day autoscaling for hosted websocket view-syncer machines based on production CPU and session affinity. No comments were available.
assessment: Varve has no hosted collaboration view-syncer fleet or session-affine websocket infrastructure. This is an upstream operations and cost optimization request.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve has no hosted collaboration view-syncer fleet or session-affine websocket infrastructure. This is an upstream operations and cost optimization request.

title: Show the fill preview live for draw strokes split past maxPointsPerShape
reason: The issue describes tldraw's capped DrawShape segmentation and its cost of merging stroke pieces during every pointer move. No comments were available.
assessment: Varve's PencilTool captures a single freehand gesture into one draft, simplifies and fits it on pointer-up, and has neither the cited per-shape point cap nor that live close-to-start fill-preview contract. The reported split-preview loss cannot occur through the same path.

The reported split-preview loss cannot occur through the same path.

title: GroupShapeUtil.getGeometry throws when a child is removed inside a transaction
reason: The report concerns tldraw's GroupShapeUtil recomputing geometry while a child index still includes a record deleted by the active transaction. No comments were available.
assessment: Varve does not use the cited GroupShapeUtil/getShapeGeometry cache contract. Its scene groups and structural renderer use a separate document model; no equivalent crash was found from this upstream implementation detail.

varveAssessment.assessment: Varve does not use the cited GroupShapeUtil/getShapeGeometry cache contract. Its scene groups and structural renderer use a separate document model; no equivalent crash was found from this upstream implementation detail.

title: Thumbnail render produces a blank or cropped picture for boards wider than the camera's minimum zoom allows
reason: The sole comment says the report was opened by mistake in place of the SDK stroke-path issue and points to the PR discussion covering the hosted blank-thumbnail behavior.
assessment: The tldraw thumbnail page fits a board through the editor's camera zoom floor, while Varve's thumbnail service computes output scale directly from render bounds and clips to that output region. No equivalent camera-minimum clamp is used in this path.

varveAssessment.assessment: The tldraw thumbnail page fits a board through the editor's camera zoom floor, while Varve's thumbnail service computes output scale directly from render bounds and clips to that output region. No equivalent camera-minimum clamp is used in this path.

title: Draw stroke spanning hundreds of thousands of units emits NUL characters in its SVG path and renders nothing
reason: Reports a tldraw freehand path formatter emitting NUL bytes only when a stroke's own extent is extremely large; the report distinguishes this from a far-translated stroke. No comments were available.
assessment: Varve renders scene paths through numeric engine geometry rather than the cited tldraw stroke SVG formatter; no corresponding NUL-producing formatter was found. This extreme-coordinate case remains a useful future robustness fixture if a local repro or malformed export appears.

title: Animation of whiteboard drawings
reason: One comment points the reporter to flash.tldraw.com; the later comment expands the use case to replaying board construction with speed control and possible GIF/video export.
assessment: Varve's Motion workspace animates authored properties over a timeline, but it does not record document mutations as a creation-history playback. The request is a potential teaching/presentation feature with distinct storage, privacy, and export scope; it should be evaluated separately from current keyframe animation rather than treated as a defect.

title: [Localization] Multiple translation issues in Simplified and Traditional Chinese
reason: The two comments direct the reporter to request access to tldraw's Lokalise project and confirm the contribution arrangement; no additional Varve terminology examples are supplied.
assessment: Varve does not currently ship a Simplified or Traditional Chinese UI locale or use the cited Lokalise contribution workflow. These terminology corrections cannot be mapped into a Varve translation catalog today; adding Chinese localization would be a separate product and localization program decision.
